requirements.description: Daily Fama-French market, SMB, HML and RF factors plus momentum UMD, joined by date to CRSP for the idiosyncratic-volatility branch. The program sorts the factor series and computes mktrf lags 1-3 before the event join (lines 559-565). The join filters SAS INTCK('WEEKDAY') TD values -262:+41, while GLM uses TD -51:+10 and the residual baseline is -51 to before -11. The fitted rows therefore also rely on upstream factor predecessor records for the lagged regressors; the exact minimum calendar start/history cannot be inferred from these relative filters alone, and the TD values are not verified exchange-session indices.

issues.description: The initial RSUBMIT block assumes an existing WRDS connection and leaves MYDIR as a commented example. The active MYDIR assignment appears only in the later ALP block, so the core remote library/path setup is not self-contained.

The bounded local SAS probe fails during TKELS initialization before reporting a version. This leaves SAS, SAS/CONNECT for RSUBMIT and SAS/STAT for PROC GLM unverified; the diagnostic does not establish a missing license.
The basic analysis reads AEPD, but no AEPD producer appears in the complete SAS source. The program instead constructs and downloads JSATC_BASEDataSet; its compatibility with AEPD is not documented.

OIYEAR is built from EAFile identifiers and return fields, but OIYEARBase keeps Q_PAR24 and later filters on it. No producer for Q_PAR24 appears in the supplied source; no proxy or replacement is assumed.
The code creates mydir.aeprevd and downloads it as ALPALL, then a later macro reads mydir.aeprevdpre to produce ALPSUM. No producer for aeprevdpre appears in the file.

The authors state that TAQ buy/sell imbalance code is not posted. The package does not supply the intraday Lee-Ready construction for AOI, effective spreads and ask depth, so the documented TAQ analyses cannot be reproduced from the supplied program alone.

The package includes core SAS construction and partial analysis blocks, but not code/data closure for the appendix options, Reg SHO, MIA, WSH, 8-K, broker-dealer leverage and Friday-effects analyses. The datasheet also points to missing main-paper Sections 3 and 4. The CUSIP file is only an identifier list, not a prepared-data bypass.

The appendix narrative gives 2006-2012 for Wall Street Horizon tests, while the Table 6 caption reports 2006-2014. The exact vendor archive, verification definition and intended sample endpoints need author confirmation.

The datasheet says Table 10 is the exception to the WRDS data route but names no alternative source or workflow. The appendix describes a t-6 to t-2 ALP window, and the referenced main-paper sections are not included.

MIA is defined as a firm-day fraction based on stock and options trading volumes following Johnson and So (2016a), but this package supplies neither the MIA file nor its calculation program and fields.

The datasheet names weekly New York Fed repo/financing data, while Table 8 describes a seasonally adjusted log change in broker-dealer leverage over 1993-2009. The current NY Fed page begins in 1998 and does not establish the pre-1998 observations or the transformation from repo data to LevFac.

Table 12 requires a Friday-effects firm-week panel at the CRSP/Compustat/TAQ intersection for 1993-2012, with prior-week price above $1, at least three prior months of prices and nonmissing prices for every day in the week. No panel construction or output code is supplied.

The SAS program defines TD with INTCK('WEEKDAY', ActDate, observation date) and applies event filters to that value. The source does not establish that this weekday-interval convention corresponds to exchange-session/trading-day indices or the appendix's externally reported TAQ/options windows; do not silently substitute another calendar convention.

actions.description: Establish the supported SAS/CONNECT and WRDS session, set the active MYDIR path, and confirm the exact source vintages, fields, units, identifiers and date coverage for each locally catalogued candidate and WRDS library.
steps: Use a supported SAS runtime and confirm SAS/STAT PROC GLM and SAS/CONNECT RSUBMIT/upload/download capability; the recorded TKELS startup error alone does not establish entitlement.
Configure the WRDS remote connection and an active MYDIR library path in the user's environment, then confirm each referenced library resolves.

For Compustat and IBES, verify underlying data vintages and point-in-time identifiers over the reported 1983-2012 samples; check quarterly lag history, FPI/actual-date fields, annual fundamentals, SIC validity and CCM link-date rules.
For CRSP, verify the daily event-window history needed for -60:+30, -41:+41 and -34:+34 windows, CRSP.DSI market returns, name-validity intervals and S&P 500 membership dates.
For Fama-French factors, verify date alignment and units for Mkt-RF, SMB, HML, RF and UMD; honor the model's actual -51:+10 fit and -51:-11 baseline despite the broader -262:+41 join.
Keep source-level broad filters (1970-2013 and -262:+41) distinct from the reported 1983-2012 event samples and each model's specific history needs.

For each CRSP/FF pull, preserve the literal SAS INTCK('WEEKDAY', ActDate, Date) filter and confirm with the authors how its values correspond to reported trading-day windows and observed exchange sessions; do not silently replace the convention.
For the factor series, account for the pre-join Mkt-RF lag1-3 construction by confirming predecessor records for each fitted observation; do not infer a calendar start date from the TD bounds alone.
validation: Record actual source names, vintage, earliest/latest usable dates, required columns and license/session availability.
Check identifiers, point-in-time link intervals, duplicate keys, merge rates, and the required lag/window observations after author filters.
Confirm factor units and date matching without executing the author's full program; do not infer population coverage from a row-one probe.
Compare code-derived INTCK('WEEKDAY') values with the authors' stated event-time convention before treating any offset as an exchange trading-day index.
Confirm upstream factor records for mktrf lags 1-3 at the earliest fitted rows, while retaining the stated -51:+10 fit and -51:<-11 residual baseline.

actions.description: Request the authors' exact upstream producers or prepared data definitions for AEPD, Q_PAR24 and mydir.aeprevdpre, including expected variables, keys, filters and ordering, before completing either analysis branch.
steps: Ask whether AEPD is an intended supplied input or an omitted transformation of JSATC_BASEDataSet, and obtain its exact producer and column mapping.
Ask which upstream step creates Q_PAR24 and how it is linked into OIYEAR/OIYEARBase; preserve the named variable until authors confirm its construction.
Ask for the producer of aeprevdpre and its relationship to the generated aeprevd/ALPALL; obtain the required sample, ordering and variables.
Incorporate only the author-confirmed upstream program or compatible prepared data in a future authorized update.
validation: Trace each confirmed output to a source producer and verify expected columns, identifiers, row keys, sample filters and order before downstream analysis.
Check that AEPD and AEPREVDPRE are actually available at the exact read locations and that Q_PAR24 is generated before it is retained or filtered.

actions.description: Request authorized TAQ input access and the authors' actual TAQ query and calculation workflow for AOI, effective spreads, ask depth and Table 12 Friday panels.
steps: Confirm the exact WRDS TAQ product, tables, date coverage, identifiers, quote/trade timestamps and available sizes for 1993-2012.
Request the supplied Lee-Ready order-direction code and the author definitions/aggregation for daily AOI, effective spread and ask depth.
Request the code for the Friday firm-week panel, including price-above-$1 prior-week rule, three-month minimum volatility history and full-week nonmissing-price rule.
Preserve the event and baseline windows t-51:-11 and t-4:-2 and the appendix sample definitions.
validation: Verify raw trade/quote timestamps, identifiers, effective-spread and depth variables, and daily aggregation on author-designated observations.
Reconcile Friday panel row counts and all published sample filters only after authorized input and code are supplied.

actions.description: Confirm an authorized IvyDB US route and obtain the author-compatible historical option file and options-analysis program/specification.
steps: Confirm user access and the exact IvyDB US vintage that covers 1996-2012.
Obtain the author option filters and identifier mapping for standardized at-the-money call/put pairs with common strike and expiry.
Obtain the analysis code or exact calculation specification for the t-4:-2 spread and t-51:-11 firm standardization.
validation: Verify underlying/date/strike/expiry/option-type fields, implied-volatility availability and required event/baseline days.
Compare final eligible sample period and counts with the appendix after the source and author rules are confirmed.

actions.description: Confirm the treatment-list files, extension dates and CRSP/event-identifier mapping used in the authors' 2005-2007 Reg SHO test.
steps: Obtain the exact pilot-category list and any applicable extension orders covering the study's 2005-2007 window.
Obtain the author mapping from security identifiers to event firms and the date logic for temporary exemptions.
Keep the SEC's documented original pilot period separate from the paper's 2005-2007 sample until authors confirm treatment timing.
validation: Check treatment assignments against the author-defined sample dates and identifier mapping, including boundary dates and extensions.

actions.description: Request the MIA firm-day dataset or the authors' exact Johnson and So (2016a) source fields, computation code and compatibility specification.
steps: Ask whether the authors used a prepared MIA series or constructed it from raw stock and options volume, and obtain the exact product, fields and aggregation period.
Request the estimator/code, identifier mapping, sample exclusions and the t-51:-11 standardization procedure.
validation: Confirm one row per firm-day or author-defined key, period coverage from 1993 through 2012, units and match rate to earnings dates.
Reproduce only the documented transformation and compare to author-provided checkpoints or table sample counts.

actions.description: Confirm the exact Wall Street Horizon historical earnings-date product and archive, obtain authorized records, and resolve the appendix's conflicting Table 6 endpoints.
steps: Ask which WSH historical dataset and snapshot/vintage the authors used, and confirm access to historical expected dates and public-verification status/timestamps.
Resolve whether the intended sample is 2006-2012 as stated in the narrative or 2006-2014 as stated in the Table 6 caption.
Obtain author rules for the five-trading-day public-verification cutoff and event-date/identifier matching.
validation: Verify product coverage and status/timestamp fields against the selected period.
Reconcile event counts and the narrative/table period after authors confirm the target sample.

actions.description: Verify the local WRDSSEC candidate or another authorized filing source against the authors' 1993-2012 8-K event definition and obtain the event-exclusion workflow.
steps: Confirm which local ITEMS8K date field represents the authors' filing date and whether the local product covers 1993-2012 completely.
If using SEC indexes, establish a documented source for 1993 because the published indexes begin in 1994Q3; do not assume the later index period covers the missing year.
Obtain the author's filing deduplication, firm mapping and ten-day earnings exclusion code.
validation: Check filing form, CIK, filing date, accession uniqueness and date coverage against author definitions.
Verify the earnings-window exclusion and only then compare the resulting 1993-2012 sample to the appendix count.

actions.description: Identify the exact weekly New York Fed financing series and determine whether and how it yields the appendix's quarterly LevFac variable, including the 1993-1997 history gap.
steps: Request the authors' exact February 2015 downloaded series, source fields, transformation code and seasonal adjustment for Table 8.
Clarify whether the weekly repo source is the input for LevFac or whether a separate Adrian, Etula, and Muir dealer-leverage series is required.
Identify a verified source for the 1993-1997 period, because the current official Primary Dealer Statistics page begins in 1998.
validation: Verify source-series dates, aggregation to quarterly values, seasonally adjusted log-change calculation, within-year quartile ranking and reported 1993-2009 sample period.

actions.description: Ask the authors to identify the non-WRDS Table 10 source and supporting program or confirm whether it reuses previously described data; obtain the precise ALP t-6:-2 branch.
steps: Clarify why Table 10 is the datasheet's only exception to WRDS and identify its specific source, product and data file.
Obtain the Table 10 calculation program and any omitted sample, input, or variable definitions from the referenced main-paper Sections 3 and 4.
validation: Confirm that the identified source and program reproduce the documented t-6:-2 alternative ALP window without changing the stated sample or estimand.

review_notes: Expanded checkpoint after complete datasheet, supplied 1,168-line SAS program, online appendix and exact author package review. The source package includes the CUSIP final-sample identifier list but no prepared analysis dataset; the source code does not read that list, so no analysis_only scope is supported.

All 544 frozen dependency IDs are assigned exactly once. External raw reads directly observed but omitted by the parser checklist—COMP.FUNDA, CRSPA.CCMXPF_LINKTABLE and CRSP.DSI—are included as mandatory requirements from the actual source lines 318, 311 and 374, with no invented dependency IDs.

The local SAS row-one probe proves only path readability and column presence. It records one sampled row, not file totals, population or historical coverage; local versions, product vintage, units and identifier/date compatibility remain unverified.

SAS runtime probe failed with the recorded diagnostic ERROR: TK Could not Initialize; Launch: Launch Service Load Failure; ERROR: The TKELS extension could not be loaded. This does not establish missing SAS entitlement. No SAS startup troubleshooting or author code execution was performed.

Do not equate broad code filters with study minimum history or assume SAS TD values are market sessions: supplied code filters IBES/linked events from 1970-2013 and uses SAS INTCK('WEEKDAY', ActDate, Date) for CRSP/factor relative offsets; the FF join spans TD -262:+41, while GLM uses -51:+10 and the residual baseline -51 to before -11. The factor series also creates Mkt-RF lag1-3 before joining, so predecessor factor records are needed and the exact minimum calendar start is unresolved. Appendix Table 11 reports samples beginning in 1983, and external TAQ/options windows are retained as reported pending confirmation of their mapping.

Official-source checks are candidate-route evidence only. SEC EDGAR indexes begin at 1994Q3; NY Fed Primary Dealer Statistics page begins at 1998; original Reg SHO pilot dates end in 2006 while the paper reports 2005-2007; WSH historical availability varies by dataset. None resolves the authors' exact historical vintage or mappings.
No route is marked verified. No exact output was run and no study regression or independent reconstruction was attempted.
